item.text:
**4B.9 Research Note (Bongbong Marcos, 2024)**

Working read: **mixed, leaning no**. I found **no clear evidence of a Marcos-ordered nationwide internet shutdown or a broad surveillance crackdown in 2024**. The strongest negative evidence is the continuation of **blocked sites, red-tagging, and online harassment**, while the strongest positive evidence is **connectivity expansion** and **anti-disinformation measures** rather than repression.

### Accepted claims
- **PBBM ushers Filipinos to a better, brighter, more connected “Bagong Pilipinas” with the “Philippine Domestic Submarine Cable Network” launch** | Presidential Communications Office | February 15, 2024 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-ushers-filipinos-to-a-better-brighter-more-connected-bagong-pilipinas-with-the-philippine-domestic-submarine-cable-network-launch/ | Marcos framed the PDSCN as expanding reliable, affordable internet and digital connectivity. This cuts against a finding of broad internet suppression. | QIDs: 4B.9, 4B.6

- **PBBM orders connectivity in remote, isolated communities** | Presidential Communications Office | September 9, 2024 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-orders-connectivity-in-remote-isolated-communities/ | Marcos directed DICT to expand connectivity and free Wi-Fi in remote areas. This is pro-access, not digital repression. | QIDs: 4B.9, 4B.6

- **Gov’t vows legal action vs deep fake video creators, spreaders** | Presidential Communications Office | April 26, 2024 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/govt-vows-legal-action-vs-deep-fake-video-creators-spreaders/ | The government responded to a manipulated video with investigation and possible legal action through DICT and NSC. This is a defensive anti-disinformation response, not evidence of a censorship sweep. | QIDs: 4B.9, 4B.6, 4B.5

- **PCO to designate ‘fact-check officers’ in state media to fight fake news** | Presidential Communications Office | September 9, 2024 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pco-to-designate-fact-check-officers-in-state-media-to-fight-fake-news/ | PCO said it would place fact-check officers in state media and denied a red-tagging policy. This is a limited transparency measure, but it is internal to state media rather than a safeguard for independent media. | QIDs: 4B.9, 4B.6, 4B.5

- **Philippines: Freedom on the Net 2024 Country Report** | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/philippines/freedom-net/2024 | Freedom House says internet freedom declined, 26 of 27 Duterte-era blocked websites remained blocked, and authorities imposed brief mobile-network restrictions during local festivities in late 2023 and January 2024. This is the strongest evidence of ongoing digital controls under Marcos, though not a nationwide political shutdown. | QIDs: 4B.9, 4B.6, 4B.5

- **Philippines: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report** | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/philippines/freedom-world/2024 | Freedom House says red-tagging persisted, disinformation campaigns were widespread, and political pressure on media remained. That supports a finding of digital harassment and information manipulation affecting political freedom. | QIDs: 4B.9, 4B.3, 4B.5, 4B.6

- **Philippines Digital News Report 2024** | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | June 17, 2024 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines | The report says red-tagging, libel pressure, blocked sites, and threats against journalists persisted under Marcos. This is strong independent evidence of a coercive online environment, even if not a formal shutdown policy. | QIDs: 4B.9, 4B.3, 4B.5, 4B.6

- **Red-tagging puts activists at risk** | Human Rights Watch | January 11, 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/philippines-red-tagging-puts-activists-risk | HRW said government supporters and officials used media to accuse critics of insurgent ties, putting activists at serious risk. That is direct evidence of administrative and informational harassment against opposition voices. | QIDs: 4B.9, 4B.3, 4B.5, 4B.6

- **Dangerous red-tagging of labor leaders** | Human Rights Watch | September 25, 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/25/philippines-dangerous-red-tagging-labor-leaders | HRW reported officials and security actors threatened union leaders and targeted other vulnerable groups through red-tagging. This is strong evidence of coercive pressure on political and civic activity, including online-linked intimidation. | QIDs: 4B.9, 4B.3, 4B.5, 4B.6

### Search gap
I did **not** find evidence in the sources reviewed of:
- a Marcos-ordered **nationwide internet shutdown** in 2024,
- a clear **mass surveillance program** aimed at political opponents,
- or a new, formal, Philippines-wide **digital blackout** policy.

What I did find is a narrower pattern: **preexisting site blocks, red-tagging, libel/threat pressure, and continued digital control measures**, alongside **connectivity-building and anti-disinformation steps**.
